title: Titan School Solutions - Nutrition Program Management Software - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 1920-2030 - Titan School Solutions Software permitting the purchase of said software, as described in Titan quote 1.4_OUSD (11/14/19), for management of the pupil nutrition program, for period of November 14, 2019 through June 30, 2021, in a cumulative amount not to exceed $169,356.95, for the term, with payment not to exceed the stated amount for each year of the term as listed herein: $62,378.00, via Nutrition Services Department,  for the period of November 14, 2019 through June 30, 2020; and $106,978.95 for the period of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.
headline: Approves up to $169,356.95 for Titan nutrition program software through June 2021
summary: The district is buying Titan School Solutions software to manage the student nutrition program. The cost is capped at $169,356.95 over the whole term, with yearly limits of $62,378.00 for November 2019 to June 2020 and $106,978.95 for 2020-21. It runs from November 14, 2019 through June 30, 2021, and is managed by the Nutrition Services Department.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Contract – District and Hazelrigg Claims Management Service - Workers’ Compensations Claims - Risk Management Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Contract between the District and Hazelrigg Claims Management Service, a Third-Party Administrator (“TPA”), Chino Hills, CA, for the provision of Workers’ Compensation claims adjusting services to the District, as described in the Contract, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the period of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023, in a cumulative amount not to exceed $2,090,772.00, for the term, with the service fee not to exceed the stated amount for each year of the term as stated herein: $669,760.00 for the period of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021; $696,550.00 for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022; $724,412.00, via the Risk Management Department, for the period of July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023; and with two one-year options for Contract renewal.
headline: Hires Hazelrigg to adjust workers' compensation claims, up to $2,090,772 over three years
summary: The district is hiring Hazelrigg Claims Management Service, an outside claims administrator, to handle workers' compensation claims. The total is capped at $2,090,772.00 for July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2023, with yearly limits of $669,760.00, $696,550.00 and $724,412.00. The contract also has two one-year renewal options and is paid from the district's self-insurance fund.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Transfer - Award of Bid - Milk/Dairy Products - RFP/Bid No. 19-01 - Nutrition Services Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of the transfer of the Award of Bid - Milk/Dairy Products - RFP/Bid #19-01 - from Berkeley Farms Dairy, LLC, Hayward, CA, to Crystal Creamery, Modesto, CA, with latter assuming performance for delivery of Milk/Dairy products from original awardee*, as second lowest, responsive, responsible bidder, in present amount not to exceed $250,000.00, via the Nutrition Services Department, for the remainder of School Year 2019-2020, pursuant to CA Public Contract Code Section 5106 and ratification of Superintendent of Schools. or designee. action taken as stated herein pursuant to Board Resolution No. 1920-0218, with two one-year option for renewal.
___________
*Berkeley Farms Dairy, Hayward, CA, ceased business operations.
headline: Moves $250,000 milk and dairy bid from closed Berkeley Farms to Crystal Creamery
summary: Berkeley Farms Dairy stopped doing business, so the district is moving its milk and dairy bid award to Crystal Creamery, the second-lowest responsive and responsible bidder. The amount is capped at $250,000.00 for the rest of the 2019-20 school year, with two one-year renewal options. The Superintendent already took this action, and the Board is being asked to ratify it.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Grant Award – No Kid Hungry Campaign – COVID-19 Emergency – Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Acceptance by the Board of Education of a Grant Award from the No Kid Hungry Campaign, Washington, DC, in the amount of $97,500.00, to support the critical work to distribute nutritious meals, i.e., Grab and Go Meal Distribution Program, to kids and families of the District during the COVID-19 emergency, via the Nutrition Services Department, for the period March 16, 2020 through June 30, 2020, pursuant to the terms and conditions thereof, if any.
funding_source: Grant Award - No Kid Hungry Campaign
headline: Accepts $97,500 from No Kid Hungry for grab-and-go meals during COVID-19
summary: The district is accepting a $97,500.00 grant from the No Kid Hungry Campaign. The money supports the Grab and Go Meal Distribution Program, which gives nutritious meals to kids and families during the COVID-19 emergency. The grant covers March 16, 2020 through June 30, 2020 and is managed by the Nutrition Services Department.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding (No Cost) - Center for Ecoliteracy - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between Center for Ecoliteracy (CEL), Berkeley, CA, and District, via its Nutrition Services Department, for continued Implementation of the Rethinking School Lunch Oakland (RSLO) Initiative, establishing agreements and defining shared commitment to continuing to implement the RSLO Initiative over the next three years (2020-2023), continuing the work on which partnering began in 2011, and continuing to advance many of the activities undertaken in the 2018-2019 school year outlined herein, including comprehensive school food innovations and associated educational programs in the District, at no cost to the District.

summary: The district and the Center for Ecoliteracy are signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to keep running the Rethinking School Lunch Oakland initiative over the next three years (2020-2023). The partnership began in 2011 and covers school food innovations and related educational programs. It is at no cost to the district.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
